name: EH3D-PHOENIX-3DP
notes: EH3D-PHOENIX-3DP is the 3D printing program of the PHOENIX family. Scaffolding v0.0.1: a Cargo workspace of eight libraries (none uses a crate from crates.io; the server bridge depends by path on the common client of the suite in EH3D-COMMON, a sibling folder is needed) and a command line (printers, info, check-profile, convert, filaments, slice, project, version) that read STL, OBJ and basic 3MF models with size limits and ordered refusals, read the objects, plates and a few settings of the 3MF projects that other programs save (read only), read the headers of binary G-code and of open resin layer packages (with an estimate of the exposure; the closed resin formats are refused), write binary STL, OBJ, an own 3MF package and G-code files, hold a catalog of 120 printer profiles (FDM and resin, built from public data, every one verified = false, each saying whether its temperature limits are the maker's or the conservative ones of the program) and six generic filaments checked against a printer and a nozzle, slice a closed model into flat layers with perimeters, rectilinear, grid or gyroid infill, solid skins, bridges, plain supports, seams and variable width, estimate the time with acceleration, and write G-code for the Marlin, Klipper, RepRapFirmware and Bambu dialects with temperature limits that refuse a value instead of cutting it down, check any program against those limits, drive Moonraker and OctoPrint printers through one normalized state and one list of commands over a plain HTTP transport, and keep the settings and a client of the printer3d plugin routes of the EH3D server. Everything has been tried only against simulators written for the tests and a socket of the same computer: no real printer, server or network was used. Bambu LAN is a design marked experimental that does not connect. The slicer lays a skirt, a brim or a raft and has no tree supports, no multi-material and no print from it has run on a printer. The model of a 3D viewer (camera, picking, range of layers, lines of a plan) is the crate p3dp-viewer; its wgpu drawing is behind a feature and has never been built. A window with four tabs (Prepare, Preview, Device, Project) is written for the gui feature, with filtered lists, the plan by layers, the queue of the server with a confirmed start, shortcuts and a picture mode; its logic is tested, but it has not been built or looked at on a screen.
